problems.title: Disconnected components do not identify a global ranking
claim: The stated pairwise likelihood estimates a global paper ranking without an explicit connected-component completion rule.
analysis: Two balanced-win components \(\{1,2\}\), \(\{3,4\}\) have centered equally maximizing scores \((c,c,-c,-c)\) for every \(c\). Component offsets, and hence cross-component order, are unidentified. With \(7158\) papers and \(1000\) pairwise comparisons, at most \(2000\) papers appear, leaving at least \(5158\) untouched.
result: The likelihood alone does not uniquely determine all global ranks in the allowed sparse regime. A regularizer or completion rule adds information.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: State graph connectivity, completion/tie rules and any prior or penalty. Restrict unregularized interpretation to identifiable score differences.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a low-sample estimator specification limit, without an established error in the reported ranking.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Connected comparisons need not have a finite maximum
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, p. 4, Eq. (2) over real-valued coefficients.
claim: Connectivity alone is sometimes read as sufficient for finite unregularized score estimation.
analysis: For two papers with one observed win, the comparison graph is connected and centered log likelihood is \(\log\sigma(t)\), where \(t\) is their score difference. It increases toward zero as \(t\to\infty\), so no finite maximum is attained. The pairwise ordering itself is still supported.
result: A finite estimate requires stronger conditions or a different explicit estimator.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: A declared positive ridge penalty makes the logistic objective coercive and strictly convex, supplying a unique finite penalized estimate. This is distinct from the unregularized likelihood.
problems.impact_rationale: This is an existence qualification rather than evidence that the central empirical ordering is wrong.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
